Identity.History:
Liu Bang, later known as Emperor Gaozu of Han, founded the Han Dynasty after the collapse of the Qin Empire. Born into comparatively modest circumstances, he first served as a minor local official before becoming involved in the rebellions that erupted against Qin rule. He proved less impressive as a battlefield commander than some of his rivals, but he possessed considerable political instinct, personal charisma, and an unusual ability to recognize and employ talented subordinates. During the Chu–Han Contention, he relied heavily on figures such as Han Xin, Xiao He, and Zhang Liang to overcome the more aristocratic and militarily formidable Xiang Yu.
After his victory in 202 BCE, Liu Bang established the Han imperial order while preserving much of the effective administrative machinery inherited from Qin. He reduced some of the harsher laws and burdens associated with the previous dynasty, rewarded allies with kingdoms and titles, and gradually strengthened the authority of the central government. His reign laid the institutional foundations for the Han state and helped reconcile imperial centralization with a somewhat less severe political style than that associated with Qin.
